name: Chilli Garlic Noodles
steps: Check that the dry Hakka noodles contain eggless. Bring 2200 ml water with 6 g salt to a full boil. Cook the noodles according to their packet until just tender, usually 4–6 minutes; stir once or twice to separate them. Drain immediately, rinse briefly with cool water to halt cooking, and toss with 5 ml of the oil so the strands stay separate.

Finely mince the garlic. Slice carrot and both bell peppers into thin matchsticks. Separate the spring onion whites from the greens; thinly slice both. Mix the soy sauce, vegetarian red chilli sauce and vinegar in a small bowl so they can go into the wok together.

Heat the remaining 30 ml oil in a large wok or wide pan over medium-high heat. Add garlic and spring onion whites and stir-fry for 30–40 seconds until fragrant but not dark. Add chilli flakes for 10 seconds, then add carrot and both peppers. Stir-fry for 2–3 minutes, keeping the vegetables slightly crisp.

Pour in the mixed sauces and toss for 20 seconds. Add the drained noodles, lift and toss for 1–2 minutes so the sauce and garlic coat every strand and the noodles are hot. Taste before adding the remaining 2 g salt because soy sauce varies in saltiness. If the pan is too dry, add 15–30 ml hot water, not extra sauce.

Turn off the heat. Fold in the spring onion greens, scatter toasted sesame seeds over the noodles and divide into four bowls. Serve at once while the noodles remain springy and the vegetables retain their colour.
tips: The reviewed image shows glossy separated noodles with browned minced garlic, red and green pepper strips, carrot, spring onion and sesame. This is a dry stir-fried dish, not a gravy noodle bowl. Check the chilli sauce and noodles are vegetarian and eggless.
notes: Quantities serve four adults. Check the doneness cues in each step and adjust seasoning to taste. Jain suitability depends on your household ingredient rules.
